learning.why: Teacher showed a diagram with freezer east and compass north, and said freezer doesn't pull it. I get that cold isn't the reason now, even if I don't fully understand Earth as a magnet.

end.summary:
Mahi practised that a freely suspended magnet settles roughly north–south.
They practised matching the compass needle with N and reading E for east.
The idea that cold makes a compass point north came up several times and was corrected later using Earth as a large magnet.
Compass direction use was practised; steadiness and teach-back still need checking next time.
end.parentNote: Asha practised finding directions with Mahi using a freely suspended magnet and a compass. Mahi used the method of letting the needle stop, matching its north end with N, and then reading E; the cold-related mix-up was corrected later by referring to Earth as a large magnet (correctAfterLastSeen). At home, ask Mahi to use a compass and name north, east, south, and west after the needle settles.
